messages:
liam: Heads-up — since ~03:20 UTC ap-southeast1 warm-pool GPU joins started failing, ~32% error rate. Logs show KMS/keystore egress DENY. :eyes:

sara: seeing same, provisioning queue piling up, fallback nodes not enough to keep p95 API latency under SLO. investigating firewall rule push from yesterday.

devon: I grabbed a node log: 
```
2026-03-21T03:22:11Z ERROR keystore: handshake failed: connection reset by peer
dial tcp 10.10.12.8:443: connect: connection refused
```
Looks like privatelink target not reachable.

maria: security-bot posted a note at 03:18 about FW rule group `egress-tighten-2026-03-21` applied to apac subnets. It added deny to 0.0.0.0/0 except approved natgws — keystore connected via privatelink IP that wasn't on approved list.

amir: cost note — warm-pool churn is burning ~120 nodes idle/retry, roughly $1.8k/hr while the fleet loops. We should avoid a long rollback window.

liam: Can we get a fast exception for the keystore privatelink FQNs/IPs? Prefer allowing keystore endpoints for the ap-southeast1 keystore AZs. @sara can you coordinate with security?

sara: on it. pinged @security-bot for manual exception and opened INFRA-2345 (apac-keystore-egress-exception). Created a canary rollout: allow rule for keystore IPs in staging first.

security-bot: Automated note: request INFRA-2345 received. Owner: maria. Required approvals: fw-admin, sec-ops. ETA for manual exception after approval ~15-30m.

maria: I approve the exception for the explicitly listed privatelink IPs (10.10.12.8/32, 10.10.12.9/32). Will push a scoped allow rule to the apac firewall and track via runbook.

devon: quick mitigation: can we point keystore traffic to the regional natgw as temporary route? That avoids touching FW rules but needs route update on nodes. Risk: increased egress cost and a short TTL.

liam: Route change has broad blast radius. prefer scoped allow if possible. If approval delayed >20m, fallback to route flip with preapproved runbook.

amir: FYI if we route via natgw we'll add ~0.2ms latency and extra cost ~0.07$/node/hr but lower burn than restarts. Either way put feature-flagged fallback in the deploy.

sara: firewall exception applied to staging canary at 03:45 UTC. initial canary success: 5/5 warm-pool joins now healthy. Rolling to ap-southeast1-prod in 8m pending sec-ops signoff.

maria: sec-ops signoff provided at 03:50. Pushing to prod canary now. Monitoring tokens to detect any unusual keystore requests.

ops-bot: Alert cleared: ap-southeast1 warm-pool node join failure rate dropped from 32% -> 2% after prod canary. Tokens/sec to keystore within expected baselines.

liam: Nice. Postmortem actions: (1) update FW change playbook to include privatelink FQDN/IP mapping step, (2) add automated validation in deploy pipeline that verifies keystore endpoints are allowed before FW push, (3) add warm-pool throttling guard to avoid mass churn. Will file follow-ups.

devon: logging follow-up: capture an audit webhook for future FW pushes that includes diff + impacted subnet IDs so we can auto-block bad pushes.

maria: created tickets: INFRA-2346 (fw-change-validation), INFRA-2347 (warm-pool-safety), INFRA-2348 (audit-webhook). Adding owners and SLAs.

amir: cost calc ticket INFRA-2349 to quantify real hourly waste and recommend preemptive warm-pool size cap.

liam: Thanks everyone. I'll update on-call doc and mark escalation closed. If anyone sees regression re-open thread. :thumbsup:
